comparator.name: Bachelor Life Science and Technology
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026-2027 Teaching and Examination Regulations define one 180-EC Life Science and Technology major, with 60 EC in each year. The complete compulsory first- and second-year curricula are reproduced below at their exact component-credit level. The third year preserves the regulated 30-EC minor, 15-EC bachelor research project and 15 EC of approved major electives. The programme does not define named tracks, so no route is selected and the restricted third-year elective space is not converted into an invented specialisation. The live programme page was rechecked for the present review and continues to describe the same multidisciplinary biology–chemistry–physics–technology identity. alternatives.concept: Study molecular and cellular life through biochemistry, physiology, genetics, immunity, disease, pharmacology, introductory laboratory work, neurobiology and quantitative analysis. This is a related-fields response: it does not reproduce Groningen’s organic, inorganic and physical chemistry, optics, spectroscopy, dedicated biotechnology practicals or integrated technology sequence.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest programme is a complete molecular, cellular and biomedical related-fields response. A second programme gives the explicit bioinformatics, imaging and biophysics interests a materially more quantitative organising direction, while clearly withholding a claim to experimental biophysics. Molecular pharmacology was assessed next: Pharmacology, molecular biology and disease courses are already central to the closest route, and without medicinal chemistry or drug synthesis the substitutions do not create a genuinely different 30-EC direction. Biotechnology and sustainability were also assessed, but UCR has one broad laboratory and limited biotechnology content rather than the applied microbiology, biotechnology and sustainability sequence needed to organise another complete programme. Production therefore stops at two.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both address mammalian and molecular cell biology; UCR supplies a broader biomedical foundation rather than the target’s integrated chemistry-physics context.
Both teach programming; UCR’s course is general Python and computational problem solving rather than life-science-specific programming.
Both provide calculus foundations, while UCR’s course also introduces differential equations.
Both directly study physiology; UCR emphasizes integrated adult human systems.
Both directly study biomolecules and biochemical mechanisms; UCR does not add the target’s chemistry sequence.
Both study imaging, but UCR focuses computational image processing and computer vision rather than the target’s physical imaging and instrumentation sequence.
Both include practical microbiology, but UCR offers one broad introductory life-science laboratory rather than the target’s staged practical sequence.
Both address genetics; UCR centres human molecular pathology and does not reproduce the target’s full evolution component.
Both contribute to pharmaceutical study, but UCR teaches pharmacological mechanisms and kinetics rather than analytical chemistry.

notes.text: Groningen Life Science and Technology integrates biology with sustained organic, inorganic and physical chemistry, optics, mechanics, spectroscopy, pharmaceutical analysis, biotechnology and three dedicated practical strands. UCR can support coherent molecular/biomedical and quantitative-life-science programmes, but these are related-fields responses rather than reproductions of the complete Life Science and Technology discipline.

The UCR alternatives do not supply the target’s organic-chemistry sequence, bioinorganic chemistry, thermodynamics, optics, quantum and classical mechanics, spectroscopy, pharmaceutical analysis, staged microbiology/organic-chemistry practicals or mandatory 15-EC experimental research project. Image Processing & Computer Vision is computational and must not be read as an optics or imaging-instrumentation substitute.
